hn-50319143.s: CVE-2026-98432 is a CVSS 9.8 remote use-after-free in Linux's IPv4 TCP handshake, fixed upstream Oct 15. Ubuntu and RHEL haven't shipped a fixed kernel yet.
ex: Linux's stable kernels shipped a fix on October 11 and 15, 2026 for CVE-2026-98432, a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP handshake that a remote, unauthenticated peer can reach. The kernel's own CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) scores it CVSS 3.1 9.8, Critical. The fixed releases are 5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10, and 7.3, and the bug goes back to Linux 4.4. The upstream fix is a four-line change, but most servers run a distribution's kernel, and as of 5:15 PM CDT, October 31, Ubuntu's tracker still reads "Vulnerable" for its kernel on every release, and Red Hat, which now rates the bug Critical too, lists RHEL 8, 9, and 10 as affected with no fix. Why it's urgent: the bug sits in code every Linux server runs when it accepts an IPv4 TCP connection, before any application sees the connection.

hn-50318871.t: GPT-5.6 Sol can beat Factorio on peaceful mode
hn-50318871.s: Previously: We got Claude Code playing Factorio, Towards beating Factorio autonomously, and Faketorio: an agent testbed
ex: Previously: We got Claude Code playing Factorio, Towards beating Factorio autonomously, and Faketorio: an agent testbed I got GPT-5.6 Sol, running in Codex with low thinking level, to complete a peaceful (i.e. no biters) Factorio run in 13.5 hours of game time: Similar to my previous post, this run used a game manager to allow Sol/Codex to interact with the game via a small library (though in this run it was Python rather than Bash). The library allows the model to play the game programmatically while enforcing the same restrictions that human players face when using the GUI (e.g. reach of the player, fog of war). Observing the run was fascinating: Sol exceeded my expectations in some areas while also showing clear weaknesses in others.

hn-50316531.t: Malware uses LLMs to rank victims by how much they're worth
hn-50316531.s: The self-deleting VOLTA infostealer steals credentials, sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets. Then, it uses LLMs to profile victims and rank their most valuable assets.
ex: There is a new idea in the cybercrime world — cast a wide net, steal everything, and let AI sort out the specifics. A new malware self-named “VOLTA-AUTODOXER,” surfaced through the CAIRN research effort, is a self-deleting Windows infostealer that augments its post-theft workflow with an LLM-powered victim-profiling stage. The bundle is serialized and POSTed to OpenRouter under a system prompt that instructs the model to act as "a forensic intelligence analyst drafting a target assessment." The required output includes a section titled “WHAT THEY'RE WORTH” with valuables ranked by monetization with a low/medium/high tier, and a section on “THEIR OPSEC” containing an assessment of the victim's security posture and password hygiene. The model is the operator's triage analyst; it turns a raw credential log into a prioritized and citation-backed dossier of the victim and their monetizable assets.

hn-50320255.t: Anthropic takes steps to block Claude from reverse-engineering video games
hn-50320255.s: The restrictions are so broad that they're even hurting legitimate game developers and preventing basic troubleshooting tasks.
ex: According to reporting from Tom's Hardware, Anthropic's Claude AI has quietly started restricting the kinds of work it will do, including modding, decompiling, or reverse-engineering video game code. And though there has as yet been no official announcement about why, the reason is still pretty obvious. The video game community has been in the news a lot lately, first because of the GTA6 leaks that went mega-viral and spurred Take-Two Interactive into getting subpoenas against both Microsoft and Discord in the hopes of finding the responsible parties, and next because the hacking and modding community discovered how much easier AI makes their job. First, game decompilers went into overdrive, playing around with the source code of multiple different video games to, for example, put Nintendo's Mario inside the dark gothic world of Elden Ring, or import Spider-Man into the Batman: Arkham City game, seamlessly blending the mechanics of one character into the world of another.

hn-50314699.t: Do the math: How we took over ChatGPT accounts
hn-50314699.s: In October 2026, we found a way to turn an ordinary public ChatGPT share into attacker-controlled JavaScript running inside the signed-in session of whoever opened it.
ex: In October 2026, we found a way to turn an ordinary public ChatGPT share into attacker-controlled JavaScript running inside the signed-in session of whoever opened it. An attacker could create a malicious conversation, publish it using ChatGPT's normal sharing feature, and send the link to another user. When the victim opened the share, the payload executed as chatgpt.com with access to the victim's authenticated web session. We confirmed that this code could enumerate the victim's conversation list, retrieve content from a private conversation that had never been shared with the attacker, and send data from that conversation to an external server. The payload was not limited to modifying the page or displaying an alert—it could directly call ChatGPT's authenticated APIs as the victim, essentially allowing us to take over the victim's ChatGPT account. The victim did not need to install an App, join a Project, paste code, or open developer tools.

hn-50310398.t: Sanstun: A sans-IO, parallel-friendly WireGuard implementation in Rust
hn-50310398.s: Our sans-IO WireGuard implementation in Rust, optimized for ease of use, security and performance through a parallel-friendly and idiomatic API.
ex: Today, we are announcing sanstun: a sans-IO Rust implementation of the WireGuard® state machine, optimized for ease of use, security and performance through a parallel-friendly and idiomatic API. sans-IO is the idea that you design your system such that IO and side-effects are cleanly separated from the state and "business logic". The IO in sans-IO doesn't just mean file or network IO. It also includes things like time and randomness! Due to their lack of side-effects, sans-IO components compose very well and are relatively easy to test. The design also avoids problems like function coloring and plays well with Rust's ownership rules. The code examples and references in this post are in Rust but sans-IO isn't Rust-specific at all. Its patterns and ideas can be applied in any language. For a more in-depth explanation, our sans-IO post is a good place to start. When we first built Firezone, we reached for boringtun as our WireGuard implementation.

ex: CONTRA NES native port — running in your browser via WebAssembly Loading… Choose a game Play on this computer Host online 2-player game Join Waiting… Copy invite link Start game Back Press Enter (or tap START ) to begin. ← ↑ → ↓ move · A / Space jump · S fire · Enter Start · Shift Select On-screen: A = jump · B = fire Online: both players use these same keys on their own computer. Player 1 picks 2 PLAYERS with Shift on the title screen. Nintendo ⇓ ⇓ ⇓ ⇓ WOOHOO! HOORAY FOR NOSTALGIA!!! Based on vermiceli's annotated disassembly of Contra: https://github.com/vermiceli/nes-contra-us . Thanks for the great work. I ported it in two steps. First to C: the game logic is translated routine by routine from the 6502 assembly, and checked frame by frame against the original in the Mesen emulator. Then the C code to WebAssembly so it runs in the browser. The cherry on top: online multiplayer, so two players can play co-op over the internet. Source: https://github.com/epoyraz/nes-contra-us

hn-50304122.t: Cisco gives engineer unlimited AI tokens to rewrite legacy code
hn-50304122.s: Meet Paddy, the 27-year-old Cisco’s president calls an “energizer bunny.” He’s been given unlimited AI tokens and told to “go nuts.”
ex: Gen Z can’t catch a break. Entry-level jobs are vanishing; some 40% of bosses say they plan to hire fewer grads because AI can do the job cheaper, and young workers are routinely slammed for showing up late and refusing to put in overtime for free. Cisco’s president and chief product officer Jeetu Patel isn’t buying it—he’s just handed one of the company’s biggest jobs to a 27-year-old he found hidden in the org chart “five levels” below him. “I’ve given him unlimited tokens because he’s going to refactor code,” Patel told Fortune at a small roundtable dinner. “So I’m like, you can go, you can go nuts.” The “him” is Padmanabhan Krishnamurthy, or “Paddy,” as Patel affectionately calls him. He joined Cisco in 2025 after the $429 billion tech giant acquired EzDubs, the real-time translation startup Krishnamurthy cofounded in 2023.

hn-50307183.s: The move came after 404 Media published an investigation into how Proton CEO Andy Yen was aggressively pushing AI across Proton despite security concerns and the culture of fear he has created.
ex: On Friday, Andy Yen, the CEO of Proton, cancelled a series of nearly company-wide ‘re-interviews’ that would have forced employees to explain how they are using AI, with the clear intention that they may be fired if not using it enough in the eyes of Proton leadership, according to six current Proton employees and audio of an around two hour all-hands meeting obtained by 404 Media. The move came after 404 Media published an investigation on Thursday, which showed how Yen was aggressively pushing AI across Proton, in some cases despite security concerns from employees. In one exchange, an employee in the company’s security Slack channel urged Proton to at least take a few days to pentest newly written code before pushing it live. “That’s bullshit and loser thinking. Of course it’s possible to be fast and secure,” Yen wrote in the channel at the end of August.

hn-50316103.t: Retired professor arrested for blocking delivery robot. Will do it again
hn-50316103.s: One Philadelphia woman’s single-minded quest to inconvenience delivery robots got her handcuffed by police.
ex: October 14 wasn’t the first time Carolyn Marvin put herself in front of an autonomous delivery robot. It had become, since the wheeled little food vessels were unleashed upon certain parts of Philadelphia, a habit for the 78-year-old: standing in front of one of the robots when she encountered it rolling on the sidewalk, delaying it for a few minutes from delivering its precious lunchtime cargo. But it was the first time that Marvin, a retired University of Pennsylvania communications professor, was arrested for doing it — in a case that she says raises profound questions about public space and the legal protections extended to robots in our increasingly tech-dominated world. “I was under the impression that I had more rights than the robot did,” Marvin said, laughing. Uber Eats launched its self-driving robot delivery fleet in Philly in March, making it the fourth city where meals can be delivered via robot.

hn-50311311.t: Anthropic to receive high 'junk' rating from credit agencies following IPO
hn-50311311.s: Blackstone's forecast is just a prediction, but naturally, a high junk rating would make it more difficult and costlier for Anthropic to raise the money to keep funding its massive spending that has…
ex: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE. Anthropic is expected to receive a high “junk” rating from credit rating agencies following its initial public offering, according to a report from the Financial Times. The FT says the investment giant Blackstone, the anchor investor in a recent $63 billion deal to finance Anthropic’s chips, told investors in the deal that it expects the AI lab to receive a “high” junk rating after its IPO. Previously, the FT notes, Blackstone had said the opposite: that the Claude maker would receive an investment-grade rating (indicating low risk for lenders) before 2027 rolls around. Now Blackstone expects double B range rating, the top tier of speculative “junk” grade, according to the reporting. TechCrunch reached out to Anthropic and Blackstone but both declined to comment.

hn-50317331.t: A USB-C LTE modem that gives my computer a phone line
hn-50317331.s: A phone line over USB-C: LTE data, SMS and voice calls with the call audio on USB. A 4-layer KiCad board designed by Koppar from a one-page spec.
ex: A 4-layer board that gives a computer its own phone line: LTE data, SMS and voice calls, with the call audio on USB. Plug in a nano-SIM and one USB-C cable, and the computer can answer a call through your headset, hand it to a script or an AI agent, or send a text. The board was designed by Koppar from a one-page spec (spec.txt), then reviewed part by part against the datasheets. One USB-C cable, and the computer sees three ordinary devices through the on-board USB hub: There is no battery, screen or speaker. Three LEDs show NET (green), RING (amber) and CALL (blue). Power is 5 V from USB-C, a 3.8 V / 3 A buck for the module's 2 A transmit bursts, and 3.3 V for the hub, the RP2040 and its flash. Board. Upload board/fab/gerbers.zip to JLCPCB: 4 layers, 1.6 mm, stackup JLC04161H-3313 (the antenna feeds are 49 Ω on it). Every via is 0.45 / 0.2 mm and none sits in a pad, so pick Min via hole size 0.2mm/(0.3/0.35mm) and Via covering: Plugged: no via-in-pad, no extra options. Assembly.

hn-50319510.t: HackerTube: YouTube built from videos recommended by HN
hn-50319510.s: It was Friday night at 11pm, I was tired, I went to YouTube to watch something and realized that I was looking at an enshittified wall of slop.
ex: It was Friday night at 11pm, I was tired, I went to YouTube to watch something and realized that I was looking at an enshittified wall of slop. Insanely exaggerated thumbnails, dumb recommendations of the same tired topics, truly terrible idiocracy-grade content. I'm sure this algorithm works well for the median person on the internet, but it definitely does not work for me. So this morning (Saturday) I took a hold of my Opus 5.5 and gave it the task: Let's write our own YouTube clone based on whatever videos have been recommended on Hacker News. And Opus came back with: hackertube.org! Opus downloaded all comments of HackerNews, filtered them down, ran Sonnet over them in a workflow, got rid of spam and low grade content, and narrowed them down to just 40K comments recommending a YouTube video. In total, we get 6,454 YouTube videos that have been recommended by a few people on HN from 2007-2026 across 150 topics.

hn-50315782.t: A language model that lives in a boot sector
hn-50315782.s: A language model that lives in a boot sector
ex: The MBR is 512 bytes of hand written asm. It loads an 11.5 KB int8 model from the next 23 sectors and runs it in 16-bit real mode on a 386. No OS, no C runtime, nothing. The machine wakes up and dreams a Linux boot log: timestamps, PCI bars, ACPI events for hardware that never existed. Build thread: https://x.com/krlntn/status/2116514628457185757 With 8 chars of context and one hidden layer this is roughly the quality you get: disk.img is a normal boot image. dd it to a USB stick and boot any BIOS box if you have one. It only reads its own sectors. corpusgen.py makes 3 MB of fake dmesg. One kernel version and one disk per boot session, because real boot logs repeat themselves and that repetition is what makes a tiny model look sane. train.py trains the model (char embeddings, one hidden layer, softmax) and quantizes everything to int8 with power-of-two scales, so the boot sector can do the whole forward pass with imul and a single idiv.

hn-50315990.t: AI startup hacks Anthropic, gains access to employee details, internal messages
hn-50315990.s: An AI startup hacked Anthropic within 12 hours and accessed employee details and internal messages. The breach exposed both personnel information and private company communications.
ex: A cybersecurity startup called Cathedral gained access to sensitive internal systems at Anthropic in less than 12 hours, exposing employee information, salary details, job offers and internal messages discussing the company's advanced AI models. The incident was discovered during a security test conducted under Anthropic's programme for outside researchers to identify vulnerabilities. According to a draft report reviewed by The Washington Post, Cathedral used AI agents to find weaknesses in business software used by Anthropic for administrative and sales tasks. The researchers found ways to access internal data, including meeting transcripts and Slack messages, after running their agents for less than 12 hours. Cathedral was founded by former members of the US Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) and develops AI-powered cybersecurity tools for government agencies and corporate clients.

gh-1440705679.s: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System
ex: dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for DeepSeek Harness. It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person. It is also a way of working with an agent: take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible. An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. docs/000-philosophy.md explains the principle and what it asks of the operator. Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent: It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything.

gh-1439372976.s: 244 pixel art effects, every one a small piece of code. Plus a Claude Code skill to make your own.
ex: 244 pixel art effects and animations, every one a small piece of code. Fire, explosions, magic, weather, UI, pickups, critters and more. Play them live, recolor and mirror them, drop them into a browser game, or export sprite sheets for any engine. Plus a Claude Code skill that makes new ones the way a picky pixel artist would: draft, render, look, refine. Every effect that involves a character is acted out: he winds up, lets go, freezes on contact and recovers, and a target takes the hit. Twelve whole moves chain the effects into attacks from wind-up to recovery. open the gallery · catalog · acting · the skill · make your own · how it works The method is Hugo Duprez's, from How to make (good) pixel art effects with Claude: code is clay, trust your eyes, feed your references. His open-source effects at Sprite Fusion set the bar, and src/core/sim.js and the effects that say so at the top adapt his code. This repo is our take on the idea at library scale, with a skill to keep going.
